reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G3-MG-Q4-Harden (mat_g3_mg_q4_0), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The sample packet fulfills the MATATAG competency to describe and draw the effect of two-direction multi-step slides. Items test conceptual understanding of translation preservation (e.g., "A rectangle undergoes a two-direction slide: 4 units right and 2 units up. Does the orientation or shape of the rectangle change?"), multi-step directional combination (e.g., "A figure slides 2 spaces left, then 1 more space left, then 4 spaces up. What is the total movement in the two directions?"), and determining resulting drawn grid points (e.g., "A circle at grid coordinate (2, 4) slides 5 spaces right and 1 space down. At what grid point will the circle be drawn?").

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The packet covers all essential facets of the competency: movement identification ("A shape slides 5 spaces to the left and 2 spaces down. What type of movement is this?"), direction counting ("A shape moves 2 spaces right AND 3 spaces up. How many directions did it slide?"), multi-step combination along an axis ("A figure slides 2 spaces left, then 1 more space left, then 4 spaces up. What is the total movement in the two directions?"), resulting grid point determination ("A shape starts at position (5, 5). It undergoes a two-direction slide: 2 spaces left and 3 spaces down. What is the new position?"), and reverse displacement calculation ("A point moves from (1, 1) to (4, 5). How many units right and how many units up did it slide?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The vocabulary and syntax are well-calibrated for Grade 3 Quarter 4 students. Sentences are concise, direct, and avoid complex clauses or heavy reading loads. Questions like "A circle at grid coordinate (2, 4) slides 5 spaces right and 1 space down. At what grid point will the circle be drawn?" and "A point moves from (1, 1) to (4, 5). How many units right and how many units up did it slide?" focus cognitive effort squarely on spatial reasoning and basic counting/arithmetic.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The generator provides a robust variety of problem archetypes: classification of motion types ("A shape slides 5 spaces to the left and 2 spaces down. What type of movement is this?"), invariant property verification ("A rectangle undergoes a two-direction slide: 4 units right and 2 units up. Does the orientation or shape of the rectangle change?"), multi-step displacement synthesis ("A figure slides 2 spaces left, then 1 more space left, then 4 spaces up. What is the total movement in the two directions?"), forward coordinate mapping ("A shape starts at position (5, 5). It undergoes a two-direction slide: 2 spaces left and 3 spaces down. What is the new position?"), and inverse coordinate displacement ("A point moves from (1, 1) to (4, 5). How many units right and how many units up did it slide?").

competency_alignment.rationale: All items remain strictly within the boundaries of the MATATAG Grade 3 geometry domain. The questions deal only with basic shapes, first-quadrant grid positions, and two-direction slides without exceeding into negative coordinates, formal coordinate geometry formulas, or unintroduced transformations. Options in items like "A shape slides 5 spaces to the left and 2 spaces down. What type of movement is this?" use grade-appropriate terminology such as 'slide (translation)', 'turn (rotation)', and 'flip (reflection)'.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: All coordinates and translation distances use manageable single-digit whole numbers within 1 to 9 (e.g., in "A point moves from (1, 1) to (4, 5). How many units right and how many units up did it slide?" and "A shape starts at position (5, 5). It undergoes a two-direction slide: 2 spaces left and 3 spaces down. What is the new position?"). This scale allows students to easily visualize or draw the movements on standard elementary grid paper without computational overburden.
